statutoryAuthority.ruleStatement: For an absolute pardon for a crime the person did not commit, the Secretary of the Commonwealth transmits the pardon to the proper circuit court. Upon receipt under 2.2-402, the court shall enter an order requiring expungement of the relevant records. This is not the ordinary acquittal/dismissal petition. Transmission to State Police remains a court/clerk act.

Do not select CC-1472, CC-1473 or CC-1474A as a substitute without the applicable actual source and adopted treatment.
Do not invent participant signature, fee, service or contact requirements from the ordinary petition procedure.
Do not use the separately published December 1, 2026 statutory version for this adopted review.

statutoryAuthority.ruleStatement: Va. Code 19.2-392.2(I): upon receiving a copy pursuant to 2.2-402 of an absolute pardon for the commission of a crime that a person did not commit, the court shall enter an order requiring expungement of the police and court records relating to the charge and conviction; the order states that expungement is ordered under this subsection and is then treated as provided in subsection (K). That court duty is branch A and needs no petition. Where the participant is instead pursuing the filing path, the Supreme Court of Virginia publishes CC-1472 as the petition for this same subsection, and that is branch B.
doNotImport: Do not use CC-1473 or import the subsection (A) acquittal-or-dismissal petition procedure into this subsection (I) route.
Do not import subsection (D)'s Commonwealth notice period into this route; CC-1472's own service requirement is a copy on the Commonwealth's Attorney, which is a different thing.
Do not represent this packet as obtaining, classifying, or applying for the pardon itself.
Do not make the branch B petition a prerequisite to the branch A court duty.
Do not state or imply a fee exemption. Subsection (I) contains none, and CC-1472's own checklist says to file with all applicable fees and costs.
Do not require email for CC-1472: the official instruction inventory has no email destination. Preserve legacy email values without printing them on an invented form line.

participantChecklist.text: Confirm from the pardon document itself that it says both absolute pardon and that the crime was one you did not commit.
Check first whether the court has already received the pardon copy from the Secretary of the Commonwealth. If it has, the court must enter the expungement order without a petition from you.
Fill CC-1472 elements 4 to 9 from the pardon order, the court file and your CCRE record; do not guess.
Leave the court case number blank if you do not know it, and leave the hearing date and clerk signature lines entirely to the clerk.
Sign and date CC-1472 personally, or have your attorney sign, and select which role signed.
Attach a copy of the order granting the absolute pardon.
Ask the clerk whether that court requires a CC-1416 cover sheet, and what fees and costs apply.
Serve a copy of the petition and its attachments on the Commonwealth's Attorney for the county or city where you file.
File the original with the clerk of the circuit court of the county or city where the charge was disposed of.
